- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially +0.23 or +0.27) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct.
- Underestimate when sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., -0.16 or -0.11) — model ignores downward pressure.
- Lag in response to recent price highs — model often peaks too early or too late relative to true trend.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility, fails to smoothly revert to historical mean.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate in early periods (first 5–7 days) after a spike, then underestimate later.
- Sentiment-driven adjustment: if sentiment is positive (e.g., +0.23) in last 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overconfidence.
- Avoid “sudden drop” after spike — model often fails to anticipate sharp reversals following high sentiment peaks.
